findings.location: tests/promptRefinerShadowLiveAdapter.test.mjs:271-278 ("no shipped entry point imports the live adapter")
findings.claim: The entry-point guard backing "route는 live adapter를 import하지 않는다" was relaxed from a whole-file substring match to two import-statement regexes, so a re-export (`export ... from "...promptRefinerShadowLiveAdapter"`) or a `require()` of the adapter in a shipped entry point now passes the guard while still loading the adapter at runtime.
findings.reproduction: Append `export * from "@/lib/promptRefinerShadowLiveAdapter";` to app/api/admin/prompt-refiner/shadow-run/route.ts, then run `node --conditions=react-server --import tsx --test tests/promptRefinerShadowLiveAdapter.test.mjs`. The test still reports 0 failures (offenders === []), although the route module now pulls in the adapter; the pre-change substring check failed on exactly this input. The relaxation was needed only because lib/promptRefinerShadowRunContract.ts:68 now contains the adapter path as a manifest string, which can be handled by exempting that one declaration instead of weakening the pattern for all files.

findings.claim: The sweeper can close at most one stale intent per run — closing the first latches the run to `stopped_unknown`, after which every remaining stale intent refuses with PROMPT_REFINER_SHADOW_RUN_TERMINAL, is silently swallowed at line 899-909, and can never become terminal nor be surfaced again, contradicting the documented "최대 16건을 unknown_after_dispatch로 terminal 처리" boundary.
findings.reproduction: In tests/integration/prompt-refiner-shadow-run.db.test.ts, after approveStage()/approveRun(), call `dispatch({requestId:"a",caseIndex:0})` and `dispatch({requestId:"b",caseIndex:1})` with no terminal in between (the writer at lines 538-684 permits a second intent while the first is open), age both rows by 61 seconds with the same trigger-disable technique the existing sweep test uses, then call `sweepPromptRefinerShadowUnknowns()`. Expected per the contract: both ids in `closedUnknownAttemptIds`. Actual: exactly one id; the other attempt stays `status='dispatch_intent'` forever (the run guard rejects any further update of a terminal run), and a second sweep returns `staleCandidates: 0` because the query filter at line 884 excludes attempts of stopped runs, while `consumedWithoutAttempt` does not list it either — so the open intent is invisible to the operator.

findings.claim: The 60-second unknown cutoff is computed from the application clock (`Date.now()`) and compared against the DB-clock-written `dispatchIntentAt`, unlike every other boundary in this writer which reads `clock_timestamp()` via `dbClock()`; app-clock skew can therefore close an in-flight dispatch early and irreversibly latch the one-shot run to `stopped_unknown`.
findings.reproduction: In the DB integration test, after `dispatch({requestId:"x",caseIndex:0})`, stub the process clock (`const real = Date.now; Date.now = () => real() + 120_000;`) and call `sweepPromptRefinerShadowUnknowns()`. Expected: no candidates, because `SELECT clock_timestamp()` shows well under 60 s since `dispatchIntentAt`. Actual: the fresh intent is closed as `unknown_after_dispatch` and the run latches `stopped_unknown`, which no code path can undo.

findings.claim: Both new protected-table entries cite `docs/policy/prompt-refiner-observability.md §8`, which is the "다음 연결 단계" roadmap list; the invariants for these two tables live in §12 and in docs/ops/prompt-refiner-durable-run-writer-contract.md.
findings.reproduction: `rg -n "^## " docs/policy/prompt-refiner-observability.md` shows §8 = "다음 연결 단계" (lines 200-207, a five-item roadmap that never mentions PromptRefinerShadowRun/Attempt), while §12 (line 342 onward) is the section this change actually extended.

verdict.nextAction: Codex should restore a non-bypassable live-adapter entry-point guard, make the unknown sweeper either close or explicitly report every stale intent on a latched run, and move the cutoff to the database clock; the two documentation nits can be folded into the same revision for round 1.
